cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has a message about the gods of Babylon. Bel crouches. Nebo cowers. Their idols get loaded onto beasts and cattle.

cards.question: Bel and Nebo's idols are piled onto beasts and cattle. What does Isaiah say those idols are to the weary animal?

cards.text: Think about that, friend. You pray to a god, and your god needs a RIDE.

cards.question: Bel and Nebo can lift the heavy load off the weary animals.
Bel and Nebo can't help the animals carrying them. So where do Babylon's gods end up?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to the house of Jacob, all who are left of the house of Israel. And He flips the whole picture around.

cards.question: Babylon's gods have to be carried. What does the LORD say He has done for the house of Jacob since birth?
The LORD tells the house of Jacob that His care for them will stop once they grow old.

cards.text: He'll bear them up even when they turn gray. Friend, MY edges went soft with age, and I got slid into a junk drawer.

cards.question: The LORD promises to carry Israel, sustain them and deliver them. What does He say He has already done for them?

cards.text: Then the LORD asks, "To whom will you compare Me, that we should be alike?" Good luck with that one, friend.
Then He shows what people do. They pour out bags of gold, weigh out silver on scales, and hire a goldsmith.

cards.question: The goldsmith shapes the gold into a ___ so the people can bow down and worship.

cards.text: Then they lift it to their shoulders and carry it along. Another god that needs a RIDE.

cards.question: The people set their gold god down in its place. What does it do once it's there?

answers.text: It doesn't budge from that spot
It falls on its face at night
It slowly turns toward the east

cards.text: Not budging from one spot? I did that for YEARS in a junk drawer, and nobody ever prayed to ME.

cards.question: When the people cry out to their gold god, it answers and saves them from their troubles.

cards.text: Now the LORD calls out to transgressors: remember this, take it to heart and be brave. And remember what happened long ago.

cards.question: As He tells them to remember what happened long ago, what does the LORD say about Himself?

answers.text: He is the greatest of many gods
He needs His people to help Him

cards.text: The LORD says He declares the end from the beginning. Friend, I can't even tell you how a batch turns out until the timer goes off.

cards.question: The LORD declares the end from the beginning. What does He say about His purpose?

cards.text: Then the LORD says He's summoning someone from the east, from a far-off land.

cards.question: What picture does the LORD use for the one He summons from the east?

cards.text: He calls him a man for His purpose. Friend, I PLAN to clean my ovens early every morning, and then I meet the snooze button.

cards.question: The LORD says His plan for the man from the east might not come to pass.

cards.text: The LORD says, "Listen to Me," and calls them stubborn people, far removed from righteousness.

cards.question: The people are far removed from righteousness. What does the LORD say He is doing with His righteousness?
The LORD says His salvation will not be delayed, and He will grant salvation to ___.

cards.text: And He'll adorn Israel with His splendor. Babylon's gods got loaded on tired animals and hauled into captivity. Israel gets SPLENDOR.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke. It tells no new piece of the passage and just reacts to card 2. The joke needs to ride along on a card that also carries the next moment, such as the gods cowering and crouching together in 46:2.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about card 15's answer. It doesn't move the passage forward and works as a recap of the idol not budging. The joke should sit on a card that tells the next moment, such as the people crying out to the idol in 46:7.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Isaiah 46:2 says the gods are 'unable to relieve the burden' and doesn't say whose burden it is. The statement 'lift the heavy load off the weary animals' decides that it is the animals' burden.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Bel and Nebo can't help the animals carrying them' again decides whose burden it is, which 46:2 leaves open. The word 'So' also makes the captivity a result of that, but the text only says 'but they themselves go into captivity.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card calls Bel and Nebo 'the gods of Babylon,' but Isaiah 46:1-13 never names Babylon. This fact comes from outside the passage and has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The snooze-button joke says Papa Dorin's plans fall through. That sets up the contrast and hints that the LORD's plan will not fall through, which gives away the answer to card 8. The joke is also built on 'I have planned it' from 46:11, which hasn't been told yet, so its comparison has no setup.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card cites only Isaiah 46:13 but also retells 46:1-2: the gods loaded on tired animals and going into captivity. It also calls them 'Babylon's gods,' a name the passage never gives them. That retelling works as a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Half of the card goes back over 46:1-2, which was already covered in stop 1.

Multiple choice makes up 4 of the 6 choice cards in stop 2, and there is only one true or false and one fill in the blank. Cards 2, 4 and 6 are all multiple choice and follow the same story-then-multiple-choice pattern.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
